title.zh: 卷260 列傳四十七 姚启圣 吴兴祚 施琅
title.en: Volume 260 Biographies 47: Yao Qisheng, Wu Xingzuo, Shi Lang
title.raw: 卷260 列傳四十七 姚启圣 吴兴祚 施琅

sentences.zh: =姚啟聖=姚啟聖，字熙止，浙江會稽人。

translations.literal: Yao Qisheng, style name Xizhi, was a native of Kuaiji in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Qisheng, whose style was Xizhi, came from Kuaiji in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 少任俠自喜。

translations.literal: In youth he was chivalrous and pleased with himself.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was bold and self-assured, given to acts of chivalry.

sentences.zh: 明季為諸生。

translations.literal: In the late Ming he was a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: During the closing years of the Ming he held licentiate status.

sentences.zh: 順治初，師定江南，遊通州，為土豪所侮，乃詣軍前乞自效。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shunzhi reign, when the army pacified Jiangnan, he traveled to Tongzhou and was insulted by a local bully; he then went to the army camp to beg to serve.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shunzhi reign, after the Qing armies had pacified the lower Yangtze, he was traveling in Tongzhou when a local bully humiliated him; he went straight to the military headquarters and asked to enlist.

sentences.zh: 檄署通州知州，執土豪杖殺之，棄官歸。

translations.literal: By dispatch he was appointed acting prefect of Tongzhou; he seized the bully and beat him to death with a staff, then resigned and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting prefect of Tongzhou by military order, had the bully seized and beaten to death, then quit his post and went home.

sentences.zh: 郊行，遇二卒掠女子，故與好語，奪其刀殺之，還女子其家。

translations.literal: On an outing in the suburbs he met two soldiers robbing a woman; he deliberately spoke kindly to them, seized their blades and killed them, and returned the woman to her family.
translations.idiomatic: While out in the countryside he came upon two soldiers abducting a woman; he spoke to them pleasantly until he could snatch their swords, killed them both, and sent the woman back to her family.

sentences.zh: 去附族人，籍隸鑲紅旗漢軍。

translations.literal: He left to join a kinsman and was registered as belonging to the Bordered Red Banner Han Army.
translations.idiomatic: He went to live with a kinsman and was enrolled in the Han Army of the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 舉康熙二年八旗鄉試第一，授廣東香山知縣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi he placed first in the Eight Banners provincial examination and was appointed magistrate of Xiangshan in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Kangxi reign he took first place in the Eight Banners provincial examination and was appointed magistrate of Xiangshan in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 前政負課數万，繫獄，啟聖牒大府，悉為代償。

translations.literal: His predecessor owed tens of thousands in taxes and was imprisoned; Qisheng petitioned the provincial authorities and paid the entire sum on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: His predecessor had left tens of thousands in unpaid taxes and sat in prison; Qisheng petitioned the provincial government and paid the whole debt himself.

sentences.zh: 尋以擅開海禁，被劾奪官。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was impeached and stripped of office for opening the maritime ban on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was impeached and dismissed for having reopened maritime trade in defiance of the coastal ban.

sentences.zh: 十三年，耿精忠反，兵入浙江境，陷溫​​州傍近及台、處諸屬縣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Geng Jingzhong rebelled; his troops entered Zhejiang and captured the districts near Wenzhou and the subordinate counties of Taizhou and Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Geng Jingzhong rose in rebellion; his forces crossed into Zhejiang, taking the country around Wenzhou and the dependent counties of Taizhou and Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 聖祖命康親王杰書統師進討，啟聖與子儀募健兒數百詣軍，以策幹王。

translations.literal: The Sacred Ancestor ordered Prince Kang Jieshu to command the army in advance; Qisheng and his son Yi raised several hundred stalwart men and came to the camp to offer strategy to the prince.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Prince Kang Jieshu to lead the punitive campaign; Qisheng and his son Yi recruited several hundred fighting men, joined the army, and offered the prince their counsel.

sentences.zh: 檄署諸暨知縣，剿平紫瑯山土寇。

translations.literal: By dispatch he was appointed acting magistrate of Zhuji and pacified the bandits on Mount Zilang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting magistrate of Zhuji by military order and wiped out the bandits on Mount Zilang.

sentences.zh: 十四年，以王薦，超擢溫處道僉事。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, on the prince's recommendation, he was promoted out of turn to intendant of the Wenzhou-Chuzhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the prince recommended him for exceptional promotion to intendant of the Wenzhou-Chuzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 從都統拉哈達克松陽、宣平二縣。

translations.literal: He followed the commandant Rahadak in recovering the two counties of Songyang and Xuanping.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the commandant Rahadak in retaking Songyang and Xuanping.

sentences.zh: 十五年，偕副都統沃申、總兵陳世凱等勦賊石塘，焚其木城，斬獲甚眾，乘勝復云和。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, together with Vice Commandant Wo Shen, Regional Commander Chen Shikai, and others, he suppressed the rebels at Shitang, burned their wooden fort, killed and captured a great many, and following up the victory recovered Yunhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he joined Vice Commandant Wo Shen, Regional Commander Chen Shikai, and others in attacking the rebels at Shitang, burned their timber stockade, inflicted heavy casualties, and pressed on to retake Yunhe.

sentences.zh: 先是，精忠以書招鄭錦，錦至复拒之，將士多為內應，錦遂取泉、漳二府，據廈門。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jingzhong had summoned Zheng Jing by letter; when Jing arrived he again refused him, but many officers and soldiers acted as inside collaborators, and Jing then took the two prefectures of Quanzhou and Zhangzhou and held Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Geng Jingzhong had invited Zheng Jing by letter; when Jing came he turned him away again, yet many of Jingzhong's officers and men secretly sided with Jing, who then seized Quanzhou and Zhangzhou and occupied Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 精忠與戰，复屢敗。

translations.literal: Jingzhong fought him and again suffered repeated defeats.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong fought him again and was beaten repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 啟聖又使儀破精忠將曾養性於溫州。

translations.literal: Qisheng also had Yi defeat Jingzhong's general Zeng Yangxing at Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qisheng also sent Yi to defeat Jingzhong's general Zeng Yangxing at Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 十月，師入仙霞關，趨福建，精忠降。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the army entered Xianxia Pass and pressed into Fujian; Jingzhong surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the army passed through Xianxia Pass into Fujian, and Jingzhong surrendered.

sentences.zh: 擢啟聖福建布政使，率兵討錦。

translations.literal: Qisheng was promoted to Fujian provincial administration commissioner and led troops to attack Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Qisheng was promoted to Fujian provincial administration commissioner and led troops against Zheng Jing.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂將韓大任驍勇善戰，世稱小淮陰者也，自贛入汀，謀與錦合。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui's general Han Daren was valiant and skilled in battle; the age called him the Little Lord of Huaiyin; he entered Tingzhou from Ganzhou intending to join with Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Han Daren, a general of Wu Sangui famed for valor and called in his day the Little Lord of Huaiyin, came into Tingzhou from Ganzhou intending to link up with Zheng Jing.

sentences.zh: 啟聖說之降，簡其部卒，得死士三千人，以為親軍。

translations.literal: Qisheng persuaded him to surrender, selected from his troops, and obtained three thousand men willing to die, whom he made his personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: Qisheng talked him into surrendering, picked out the best of his men, and formed a personal guard of three thousand die-hards.

sentences.zh: 十六年，從康親王復邵武、興化，盡取漳、泉地。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he followed Prince Kang in recovering Shaowu and Xinghua and took all the territory of Zhangzhou and Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he followed Prince Kang in retaking Shaowu and Xinghua and recovering the whole of the Zhangzhou and Quanzhou region.

sentences.zh: 錦遁歸廈門。

translations.literal: Jing fled back to Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jing fled back to Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 總督郎廷佐奏啟聖與子儀屢著戰功，贍軍購馬，具甲胄弓矢，糜白金五萬，皆出私財，詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: Governor-General Lang Tingzuo memorialized that Qisheng and his son Yi had repeatedly distinguished themselves in battle, supplied the army, purchased horses, and provided armor, bows, and arrows, spending fifty thousand taels of silver, all from private funds; an edict praised them.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Lang Tingzuo reported that Qisheng and his son Yi had won repeated victories, fed the troops, bought horses, and furnished armor, bows, and arrows at a cost of fifty thousand taels of silver from their own purses; the court issued a commendation.

sentences.zh: 十七年，錦遣其將劉國軒、吳淑、阿佑等復犯漳、泉，海澄公黃芳世、都統穆赫林、提督段應舉等與戰，敗績，遂陷海澄、長泰、同安、惠安、平和諸縣。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Jing sent his generals Liu Guoxuan, Wu Shu, Ayu, and others to invade Zhangzhou and Quanzhou again; Duke of Haicheng Huang Fangshi, Commandant Muhelin, Provincial Military Commissioner Duan Yingju, and others fought them, suffered defeat, and the counties of Haicheng, Changtai, Tong'an, Hui'an, and Pinghe were lost.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Zheng Jing sent Liu Guoxuan, Wu Shu, Ayu, and other generals against Zhangzhou and Quanzhou again; Duke of Haicheng Huang Fangshi, Commandant Muhelin, Provincial Military Commissioner Duan Yingju, and others were beaten, and Haicheng, Changtai, Tong'an, Hui'an, and Pinghe fell.

sentences.zh: 詔擢啟聖福建總督，條上機宜，「請調福寧鎮兵助攻泉州，調衢州、贛州、潮州三鎮兵助攻漳州，復設漳浦、同安二總兵，增督標兵五千。

translations.literal: An edict promoted Qisheng to governor-general of Fujian; he itemized strategic plans: 'Request transfer of Funing garrison troops to assist in attacking Quanzhou, transfer of troops from the three garrisons of Quzhou, Ganzhou, and Chaozhou to assist in attacking Zhangzhou, re-establish the two regional commanders of Zhangpu and Tong'an, and increase the governor-general's personal guard by five thousand.'
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to governor-general of Fujian and laid out his plans: transfer Funing garrison troops to help take Quanzhou, bring in the Quzhou, Ganzhou, and Chaozhou garrisons against Zhangzhou, restore the regional commands at Zhangpu and Tong'an, and add five thousand men to his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 通省經制兵萬八千，申明臨陣賞罰，禁廝役佔兵額」。

translations.literal: The province's regular troops number eighteen thousand; clarify rewards and punishments on the battlefield; forbid servants and runners from occupying military quotas.'
translations.idiomatic: He set the province's regular strength at eighteen thousand, called for clear rewards and punishments in battle, and forbade servants from filling places on the rolls.

sentences.zh: 下議政王大臣議，衢、贛、潮三路皆重地，未便徵發，既增督標兵，毋庸复廣通省兵額，餘皆從其議。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the Prince Regent and grand ministers for deliberation; the three routes of Quzhou, Ganzhou, and Chaozhou were all vital posts and could not conveniently be mobilized; since the governor-general's guard had already been increased, there was no need to expand the province-wide quota further; the rest of his proposals were approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince Regent and the grand ministers considered the plan: Quzhou, Ganzhou, and Chaozhou were all critical posts and could not be stripped of troops; with the governor-general's guard already enlarged, the provincial rolls need not grow further; everything else was approved.

sentences.zh: 七月，偕海澄公黃芳度自永福進克平和、漳平。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, together with Duke of Haicheng Huang Fangdu, he advanced from Yongfu and captured Pinghe and Zhangping.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he advanced from Yongfu with Duke of Haicheng Huang Fangdu and retook Pinghe and Zhangping.

sentences.zh: 國軒等解泉州圍，進逼漳州，壁於蜈蚣嶺。

translations.literal: Guoxuan and others lifted the siege of Quanzhou, pressed toward Zhangzhou, and encamped at Wugong Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxuan lifted the siege of Quanzhou, marched on Zhangzhou, and fortified Wugong Ridge.

sentences.zh: 啟聖率壯士鍾寶、張黑子等出戰，將軍賚塔、都統沃申等夾擊，連破賊寨，斬其將鄭英、劉正璽等十餘人，國軒遁海澄，乘勝复長泰。

translations.literal: Qisheng led stalwarts Zhong Bao, Zhang Heizi, and others into battle; General Baicha, Commandant Wo Shen, and others attacked from both sides, broke rebel camps in succession, and beheaded more than ten of their generals including Zheng Ying and Liu Zhengxi; Guoxuan fled to Haicheng, and following up the victory they recovered Changtai.
translations.idiomatic: Qisheng led his champions Zhong Bao and Zhang Heizi into the field while General Baicha and Commandant Wo Shen struck from the flanks; they stormed one rebel camp after another, killed more than a dozen enemy commanders including Zheng Ying and Liu Zhengxi, drove Guoxuan back to Haicheng, and followed up by retaking Changtai.

sentences.zh: 敘功，進正一品。

translations.literal: In recording merit he was advanced to the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: For his services he was raised to the first rank.

sentences.zh: 九月，復遣儀率兵攻同安，敵棄城遁，斬其將林欽等。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he again sent Yi to lead troops against Tong'an; the enemy abandoned the city and fled, and their general Lin Qin and others were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he sent Yi against Tong'an again; the enemy abandoned the city and fled, and generals such as Lin Qin were killed.

sentences.zh: 尋偕副都統吉勒塔布、提督楊捷等進攻海澄，敗國軒於江東橋，又敗之於潮溝。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, together with Vice Commandant Jiletabu, Provincial Military Commissioner Yang Jie, and others, he advanced on Haicheng, defeated Guoxuan at Jiangdong Bridge, and defeated him again at Chao Gou.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Vice Commandant Jiletabu, Provincial Military Commissioner Yang Jie, and others in attacking Haicheng, beating Guoxuan at Jiangdong Bridge and again at Chao Gou.

sentences.zh: 十八年，國軒與淑、佑等踞郭塘、歐溪頭，欲斷江東橋以犯長泰。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Guoxuan, Shu, You, and others held Guotang and Ouxitou, intending to cut Jiangdong Bridge to invade Changtai.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Guoxuan, Shu, You, and others held Guotang and Ouxitou, planning to sever Jiangdong Bridge and strike at Changtai.

sentences.zh: 啟聖偕賚塔、捷及巡撫吳興祚等邀擊，大敗之，先後招降所置吏四百餘、兵一萬四千有奇。

translations.literal: Qisheng, together with Baicha, Jie, and Governor Wu Xingzuo and others, intercepted and routed them; in succession they induced more than four hundred appointed officials and over fourteen thousand troops to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Qisheng, Baicha, Jie, and Governor Wu Xingzuo intercepted them and won a crushing victory, inducing more than four hundred rebel officials and some fourteen thousand soldiers to surrender in the course of the campaign.

sentences.zh: 國軒等復率萬餘人謀奪榴山寨，啟聖偕賚塔及副都統石調聲擊敗之，至太平橋、潮溝，斬千餘級。

translations.literal: Guoxuan and others again led more than ten thousand men in an attempt to seize Liushan Stockade; Qisheng, together with Baicha and Vice Commandant Shi Diaosheng, defeated them; at Taiping Bridge and Chao Gou more than a thousand heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxuan rallied more than ten thousand men to retake Liushan Stockade; Qisheng, Baicha, and Vice Commandant Shi Diaosheng beat them back and killed more than a thousand men at Taiping Bridge and Chao Gou.

sentences.zh: 十九年，會賚塔等攻海澄。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he joined Baicha and others in attacking Haicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he joined Baicha and others in the assault on Haicheng.

sentences.zh: 時提督萬正色先克海壇，啟聖及總兵趙得壽、黃大來等分兵七路並進，破十九寨；

translations.literal: At that time Provincial Military Commissioner Wan Zhengse had first taken Haitan; Qisheng and Regional Commanders Zhao Deshou, Huang Dalai, and others divided their forces into seven columns and advanced together, breaking nineteen stockades;
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Military Commissioner Wan Zhengse had already taken Haitan; Qisheng and regional commanders Zhao Deshou and Huang Dalai advanced in seven columns and stormed nineteen stockades;

sentences.zh: 別遣將渡海，拔金門、廈門，降錦將朱天貴等，錦退保澎湖，盡复所陷郡縣：進兵部尚書、太子太保。

translations.literal: he separately sent generals across the sea to take Kinmen and Xiamen; Jing's generals Zhu Tiangui and others surrendered; Jing withdrew to hold Penghu; all lost prefectures and counties were recovered: he was promoted to Minister of War and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: other generals crossed the strait to seize Kinmen and Xiamen; Zheng Jing's commanders Zhu Tiangui and others surrendered; Jing fell back to Penghu; every lost prefecture and county was recovered; and Qisheng was made Minister of War and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十年，左都御史徐元文劾「啟聖疏請借司庫銀十二萬，經營取息，侵占民利；

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Left Censor-in-Chief Xu Yuanwen impeached him: 'Qisheng memorialized to borrow one hundred and twenty thousand taels from the treasury to invest for interest, encroaching on the people's profit;
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year Left Censor-in-Chief Xu Yuanwen impeached him, charging that Qisheng had asked to borrow one hundred and twenty thousand taels from the state treasury to lend at interest and thus prey on the people;

sentences.zh: 題報軍前捐銀十五萬，皆剋軍餉朘民膏而得。

translations.literal: he reported a donation of one hundred and fifty thousand taels at the front, all obtained by deducting military pay and draining the people's fat.'
translations.idiomatic: that his reported donation of one hundred and fifty thousand taels to the army had been wrung from military pay and the people's substance.

sentences.zh: 閩民極困，啟聖不能存撫，拆毀民居，築園亭水閣，日役千人，舞女歌兒充牣房闥；

translations.literal: the people of Fujian are in extreme distress, yet Qisheng cannot preserve and comfort them; he tears down common dwellings to build gardens, pavilions, and waterside towers, daily impressing a thousand laborers, with dancing girls and singing boys filling every room;
translations.idiomatic: The people of Fujian were in desperate straits while he failed to relieve them; he tore down homes to build gardens and waterside pavilions, impressed a thousand laborers a day, and filled his quarters with dancers and singers.

sentences.zh: 又強取長泰戴氏女為妾。

translations.literal: he also forcibly took the daughter of the Dai family of Changtai as a concubine.
translations.idiomatic: He had forcibly taken the daughter of the Dai family of Changtai as a concubine.

sentences.zh: 海壇進師，力為阻撓，及克廈門，又言當直取台灣。

translations.literal: when troops advanced from Haitan he strenuously obstructed them, yet after Xiamen was taken he again said Taiwan should be taken directly.
translations.idiomatic: That he had obstructed the advance from Haitan, then after Xiamen fell urged an immediate strike on Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 始欲養寇，繼欲窮兵。

translations.literal: at first he wished to nurture the rebels, then he wished to exhaust the army.
translations.idiomatic: First wanting to keep the enemy alive, then wanting to fight to exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 吳興祚、萬正色平海奏功，啟聖慚妒，妄謂正色與錦將朱天貴有約，讓海壇而去。

translations.literal: when Wu Xingzuo and Wan Zhengse reported merit for pacifying the sea, Qisheng, ashamed and jealous, falsely said Zhengse had an agreement with Jing's general Zhu Tiangui and yielded Haitan and left.
translations.idiomatic: That when Wu Xingzuo and Wan Zhengse reported their victory at sea, Qisheng, ashamed and envious, falsely claimed Zhengse had a pact with Zheng Jing's general Zhu Tiangui and had yielded Haitan.

sentences.zh: 險詐欺誣，乞敕部嚴議」。

translations.literal: he is treacherous, deceitful, and fraudulent; I beg that the ministry be ordered to deliberate strictly.'
translations.idiomatic: He was treacherous and deceitful and asked that the ministry investigate him severely.'

sentences.zh: 上令啟聖覆奏，啟聖言：「臣於康熙十七年十月進兵至鳳凰山，因一時投誠者多，犒賞不繼，與撫臣吳興祚議外省貿易，頗有微利，前督臣李率泰、經略洪承疇嘗借帑為之，遂冒昧上疏，未蒙俞允。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Qisheng to reply; Qisheng said: 'Your servant in the tenth month of the seventeenth year of Kangxi advanced to Phoenix Mountain; because for a time many came over in submission and rewards could not keep pace, I discussed with Governor Wu Xingzuo trade with other provinces, which yielded some small profit; former Governor Li Shuaitai and Commissioner Hong Chengchou had once borrowed treasury funds for this; I therefore rashly submitted a memorial, which was not granted.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Qisheng to answer in writing. He replied: 'When I advanced to Phoenix Mountain in the tenth month of the seventeenth year of Kangxi, so many men were surrendering at once that I could not keep up the rewards. Governor Wu Xingzuo and I discussed trade with other provinces, which brought a modest profit. Former governors Li Shuaitai and Hong Chengchou had borrowed treasury funds for the same purpose, and I rashly asked to do likewise; the request was denied.'

sentences.zh: 臣自入仕，京師未有產業，而軍前捐銀十五萬有奇者，香山罷官後，貿易七年，得積微貲，並臣浙江祖產變價，及親朋借貸，經年累月而後有此。

translations.literal: Since entering office your servant has had no property in the capital, yet the donation of more than one hundred and fifty thousand taels at the front came from seven years of trade after dismissal from Xiangshan, accumulating a small sum, together with the sale of ancestral property in Zhejiang and loans from kin and friends, gathered over years and months before reaching this amount.'
translations.idiomatic: I have owned no property in the capital since I entered service. The more than one hundred and fifty thousand taels I gave at the front came from seven years of trade after I left Xiangshan, the sale of my family's land in Zhejiang, and loans from friends and relatives, built up month by month over many years.'

sentences.zh: 臣於十七年七月至省，見總督官廨為耿精忠屯兵毀傷傾圮，因捐貲修整，日役不過數十，柵外員役私舍，令其自行撤除。

translations.literal: Your servant reached the province in the seventh month of the seventeenth year and saw the governor-general's yamen ruined and collapsed where Geng Jingzhong's troops had been quartered; he therefore donated funds to repair it, with no more than several tens impressed daily; private quarters of clerks and runners outside the stockade were ordered removed by their occupants themselves.'
translations.idiomatic: When I reached the province in the seventh month of the seventeenth year, Geng Jingzhong's troops had wrecked the governor-general's residence. I paid for repairs out of my own purse and never impressed more than a few dozen men a day. Clerks' private quarters outside the compound were cleared away by their owners.'

sentences.zh: 至臣妾皆有子女，年已老大，並無歌兒舞女，強取戴氏女，尤無其事。

translations.literal: As for your servant's concubines, all have children and are already advanced in years; there are no singing boys or dancing girls; the forcible taking of the Dai family's daughter is especially without foundation.'
translations.idiomatic: My concubines all have children and are well past their youth; I keep no singers or dancers; and the tale about seizing the Dai family's daughter is utterly false.'

sentences.zh: 十八年十一月，臣密陳進剿機宜，請水陸五道進兵，並未阻撓。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the eighteenth year your servant secretly submitted the plan for the advance, requesting five routes by land and sea, and did not obstruct it.'
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the eighteenth year I secretly laid out the campaign plan and asked for five land and sea columns; I never obstructed the advance.'

sentences.zh: 至得廈門即攻台灣，先於十八年九月預陳，亦非屆時發議。

translations.literal: As for attacking Taiwan as soon as Xiamen was taken, this was submitted in advance in the ninth month of the eighteenth year and was not a proposal raised only when the moment came.'
translations.idiomatic: My proposal to strike Taiwan once Xiamen fell was made in the ninth month of the eighteenth year, not improvised after the fact.'

sentences.zh: 撫臣、提臣拜疏出師，平賊首功已定，臣何所容其慚妒。

translations.literal: The governor and provincial military commissioner presented memorials and set out; the chief merit for pacifying the rebels was already settled; where could your servant harbor shame and jealousy?'
translations.idiomatic: The governor and the provincial military commissioner had already memorialized and taken the field; the chief credit for pacifying the rebels was settled; I had no room for shame or jealousy.'

sentences.zh: 朱天貴應撫投誠，天貴言之而臣始知之。

translations.literal: Zhu Tiangui came over in response to pacification; Tiangui spoke of it and only then did your servant learn of it.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tiangui surrendered to the pacification authorities; I learned of it only when Tiangui himself spoke of it.'

sentences.zh: 臣任三閩三職，雖無妒功之心，實有溺職之咎。

translations.literal: Your servant has held three posts in Fujian over three terms; though without a heart that envies merit, he truly bears the fault of neglecting duty.'
translations.idiomatic: I have held three offices in Fujian across three terms; I may not have envied others' merit, but I have indeed failed in my duties.'

sentences.zh: 乞敕部嚴議，別簡賢能。

translations.literal: I beg that the ministry be ordered to deliberate strictly and that another worthy man be selected.'
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the ministry investigate me strictly and that a worthier man be appointed in my place.'

sentences.zh: 」疏入，報聞。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, acknowledgment was returned.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was received and noted.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，敘克海澄、金​​門、廈門功，授世職拜他喇布勒哈番兼拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, in recording merit for capturing Haicheng, Kinmen, and Xiamen, he was granted a hereditary office as Batuure Baturu Han and Tuosahala Han.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year his part in taking Haicheng, Kinmen, and Xiamen was recognized with hereditary ranks of Batuure Baturu Han and Tuosahala Han.

sentences.zh: 方鄭錦屢入寇，徙濱海居民入內地，俾絕接濟、避侵掠，下令越界者罪至死，民多盪析。

translations.literal: While Zheng Jing repeatedly raided, coastal inhabitants were moved inland to cut off supplies and avoid plunder; an order made crossing the boundary punishable by death, and many people were scattered and uprooted.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zheng Jing raided again and again, coastal dwellers were moved inland to cut off his supplies and shield them from attack; anyone who crossed the boundary faced death, and families were torn apart across the region.

sentences.zh: 及禁旅班師，驅系良民子女北行，啟聖白王嚴禁。

translations.literal: When the Banner troops withdrew, they drove and bound common people's sons and daughters northward; Qisheng reported to the prince and strictly forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Banner army marched home, its men were dragging local families north as captives; Qisheng appealed to the prince and had the practice stopped.

sentences.zh: 复捐貲贖歸難民二萬餘人，並請開海界、复民業，聽降卒墾荒，民困漸蘇。

translations.literal: He again donated funds to ransom and return more than twenty thousand refugees, and also requested reopening the maritime boundary and restoring people's livelihoods, allowing surrendered soldiers to reclaim wasteland; the people's distress gradually eased.
translations.idiomatic: He paid to bring back more than twenty thousand displaced people, asked that the coastal zone be reopened and livelihoods restored, and let surrendered troops farm abandoned land; gradually the people's hardship eased.

sentences.zh: 及錦死，子克塽仍其爵，稱延平王，凡事皆決之國軒等。

translations.literal: When Jing died, his son Keshuang continued his title and was called Prince of Yanping; all affairs were decided by Guoxuan and others.
translations.idiomatic: After Zheng Jing died, his son Keshuang inherited the title of Prince of Yanping, but Guoxuan and his circle made every decision.

sentences.zh: 啟聖令知府卞永譽、張仲舉專理海疆，多以金帛間其黨與。

translations.literal: Qisheng ordered prefects Bian Yongyu and Zhang Zhongju to manage the maritime frontier exclusively, often using gold and silks to sow division among their factions.
translations.idiomatic: Qisheng put prefects Bian Yongyu and Zhang Zhongju in charge of the coast and used gold and silk lavishly to split the enemy's factions.

sentences.zh: 克塽乃遣使齎書，原稱臣入貢，不薙發登岸，如琉球、高麗例。

translations.literal: Keshuang then sent envoys bearing a letter, offering to call himself a subject and pay tribute, not to shave the head or come ashore, following the precedents of Ryukyu and Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Keshuang sent envoys with a letter offering submission and tribute on the model of Ryukyu and Korea, without shaving the head or landing on the mainland.

sentences.zh: 啟聖以聞，上不許，趣水師提督施琅進徵。

translations.literal: Qisheng reported this; the emperor did not permit it and urged Naval Commander Shi Lang to advance in conquest.
translations.idiomatic: Qisheng reported the offer; the emperor refused it and ordered Naval Commander Shi Lang to attack.

sentences.zh: 二十二年六月，瑯進攻台灣，取澎湖。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-second year Lang advanced on Taiwan and took Penghu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twenty-second year Shi Lang attacked Taiwan and seized Penghu.

sentences.zh: 啟聖駐廈門督饋運，以大舟載金、纟曾、貨、米至軍，大賚降卒，遣之歸，台民果攜貳。

translations.literal: Qisheng remained at Xiamen supervising supply transport, using large ships to carry gold, silk, goods, and grain to the army, greatly rewarding surrendered soldiers and sending them back; the people of Taiwan indeed wavered in allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Qisheng stayed at Xiamen to oversee supplies, sending great ships laden with gold, silk, goods, and grain to the fleet, richly rewarding surrendered soldiers and sending them home; the people of Taiwan began to turn away from their rulers.

sentences.zh: 復設間使克塽與國軒互相猜，眾莫為用。

translations.literal: He again set up agents to make Keshuang and Guoxuan suspect each other, and none would serve effectively.
translations.idiomatic: He also planted agents to set Keshuang and Guoxuan against each other until no one on Taiwan could act with a united will.

sentences.zh: 瑯遂定台灣，克塽、國軒等皆降。

translations.literal: Lang then pacified Taiwan; Keshuang, Guoxuan, and others all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Lang then secured Taiwan; Keshuang, Guoxuan, and the rest surrendered.

sentences.zh: 語具瑯傳。

translations.literal: The account is given in full in Lang's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The full story is told in Shi Lang's biography.

sentences.zh: 啟聖還福州，未幾，疽發背，卒。

translations.literal: Qisheng returned to Fuzhou; before long a carbuncle broke out on his back and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Qisheng returned to Fuzhou; soon afterward a carbuncle on his back killed him.

sentences.zh: 明年，部議以啟聖修繕船舶、軍械，浮冒帑金四萬七千有奇，應追繳，上念其勞，免之。

translations.literal: The next year the ministry deliberated that in repairing ships and military equipment Qisheng had falsely claimed more than forty-seven thousand taels from the treasury and should make restitution; the emperor, mindful of his labors, exempted him.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the ministry ruled that he had overclaimed more than forty-seven thousand taels for ship and arms repairs and should repay the sum; the emperor, remembering his service, waived it.

sentences.zh: 子儀，膂力絕人，雄偉與父埒。

translations.literal: His son Yi had strength beyond ordinary men and a stature as imposing as his father's.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi was prodigiously strong and as imposing in bearing as his father.

sentences.zh: 初以捐納知縣從征，累戰有功。

translations.literal: At first, as a magistrate appointed by purchase, he followed the campaign and repeatedly distinguished himself in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He had bought his way into a magistracy and joined the campaign, winning distinction in battle again and again.

sentences.zh: 康親王檄署游擊。

translations.literal: Prince Kang appointed him acting guerrilla colonel by dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kang appointed him acting guerrilla colonel by military order.

sentences.zh: 議敘，內擢郎中。

translations.literal: When merit was deliberated, he was promoted within the capital to director of a bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When his services were reviewed, he was promoted to a bureau directorship in the capital.

sentences.zh: 上以儀有才略，且自陳原以武職自效，改都督僉事，以總兵用。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Yi had talent and strategy and had himself stated that he wished to serve in a military post, changed his appointment to vice commissioner of the metropolitan guard and employed him as regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw that Yi had real ability and had asked to serve in the field; he was made vice commissioner of the metropolitan guard and used as a regional commander.

sentences.zh: 歷狼山、杭州、沅州、鶴慶諸鎮總兵，鑲紅旗漢軍副都統。

translations.literal: He served successively as regional commander of the garrisons of Langshan, Hangzhou, Yuanzhou, and Heqing, and as vice commandant of the Han Army of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He held regional commands at Langshan, Hangzhou, Yuanzhou, and Heqing, and became vice commandant of the Han Army of the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 卒，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: He died and was granted sacrificial rites and burial honors.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was granted state funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 鍾寶，少業屠，流為盜。

translations.literal: Zhong Bao in youth practiced butchery and drifted into banditry.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Bao had been a butcher in his youth and drifted into banditry.

sentences.zh: 啟聖令香山，招之降。

translations.literal: When Qisheng was magistrate of Xiangshan, he induced him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: While Qisheng was magistrate of Xiangshan, he persuaded Bao to surrender.

sentences.zh: 後啟聖徵福建，寶偕同降者二十人隸麾下，每戰輒當前，所向有功。

translations.literal: Later, when Qisheng campaigned in Fujian, Bao together with twenty others who had surrendered came under his command; in every battle he took the front and wherever he went achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Qisheng marched into Fujian, Bao and twenty other former rebels joined his staff; in every fight he led the charge and won success.

sentences.zh: 累進秩都督僉事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted in rank to vice commissioner of the metropolitan guard.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to vice commissioner of the metropolitan guard.

sentences.zh: 啟聖卒，遂歸。

translations.literal: When Qisheng died, he then returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After Qisheng died, he went home.

sentences.zh: 後數年，部議注官，授潼關參將，遷靖邊協副將。

translations.literal: Several years later, after ministry deliberation he was registered for office, appointed garrison colonel of Tongguan, and transferred to vice commander of the Jingbian Brigade.
translations.idiomatic: Years later the ministry restored him to the rolls, made him garrison colonel of Tongguan, and then vice commander of the Jingbian Brigade.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 寶撫兵民有恩，稱為鍾佛子。

translations.literal: Bao treated soldiers and civilians with kindness and was called Master Buddha Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: He treated soldiers and civilians with kindness and was known as Master Buddha Zhong.

sentences.zh: 韓大任，降後入覲，聖祖以其為三桂將，留為內務府包衣參領。

translations.literal: Han Daren, after surrendering, came to audience; the Sacred Ancestor, because he had been a general of Sangui, retained him as a company commander of the Imperial Household Department's bond servants.
translations.idiomatic: After Han Daren surrendered he was received at court; because he had served Wu Sangui, the emperor kept him on the staff of the Imperial Household Department as a bond-servant company commander.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，從佟國綱徵噶爾丹，次烏闌布通，伏發，國綱歿於陣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he followed Tong Guogang in campaigning against Galdan; they halted at Ulan Butong; an ambush was sprung and Guogang died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he followed Tong Guogang against Galdan; at Ulan Butong the enemy sprang an ambush and Guogang was killed in the field.

sentences.zh: 大任驚曰：「吾聞臨陣失帥，兵家大罪。

translations.literal: Daren exclaimed in alarm: 'I have heard that to lose one's commander in battle is the gravest fault in warfare.'
translations.idiomatic: Daren cried out in alarm: 'I have heard that losing one's commander in battle is the gravest fault in war.'

sentences.zh: 吾以叛逆之黨，蒙恩不死。

translations.literal: I, of the party of rebellion, received grace and was not put to death.'
translations.idiomatic: I belonged to the rebels, yet the court spared my life.'

sentences.zh: 今豈可坐必死之律，復對獄吏乎？

translations.literal: How can I now sit under a law that means certain death and face the prison clerks again?'
translations.idiomatic: How can I now accept a sentence that means certain death and face the jailers again?'

sentences.zh: 」因馳入賊陣，手刃數十人，死之。

translations.literal: With that he galloped into the enemy ranks, personally killed several tens of men, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He charged into the enemy line, killed dozens of men with his own hand, and fell dead.

sentences.zh: =吳興祚=吳興祚，字伯成，漢軍正紅旗人，原籍浙江山陰。

translations.literal: Wu Xingzuo, style name Bocheng, was a man of the Han Army of the Plain Red Banner, originally from Shanyin in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xingzuo, whose style was Bocheng, belonged to the Han Army of the Plain Red Banner and came originally from Shanyin in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 父執忠，客禮親王代善幕，授頭等護衛。

translations.literal: His father Zhizhong, received as a guest at Prince Dai Shan's establishment, was appointed a first-class bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhizhong had served Prince Dai Shan as a guest officer and was appointed a first-class bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 興祚自貢生授江西萍鄉知縣。

translations.literal: Xingzuo, from presented scholar status, was appointed magistrate of Pingxiang in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzuo, a presented scholar, was appointed magistrate of Pingxiang in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 金聲桓叛，郡縣多被寇，萍鄉以有備獨完。

translations.literal: When Jin Shengwan rebelled, many prefectures and counties were ravaged by bandits; Pingxiang alone remained intact because it had prepared defenses.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Shengwan rose in rebellion, bandits overran prefectures and counties throughout the region, but Pingxiang alone was spared because it had taken precautions.

sentences.zh: 坐事罷。

translations.literal: He was dismissed on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed from office for an offense.

sentences.zh: 旋以守禦功复官，授山西大寧知縣，遷山東沂州知州。

translations.literal: Soon, on merit for defending against attack, he was restored to office, appointed magistrate of Daning in Shanxi, and transferred to be prefect of Yizhou in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reinstated for his success in defense, appointed magistrate of Daning in Shanxi, and later promoted to prefect of Yizhou in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 白蓮教嘯聚為患，興祚開諭散遣之。

translations.literal: The White Lotus sect gathered in uproar and became a menace; Xingzuo opened counsel and persuaded them to disperse.
translations.idiomatic: When the White Lotus sect mustered in rebellion, Xingzuo reasoned with the followers and persuaded them to disband.

sentences.zh: 复坐事降補江南無錫知縣。

translations.literal: Again, on account of an offense he was demoted and assigned as magistrate of Wuxi in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted again for an offense and assigned as magistrate of Wuxi in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 縣吏虧庫帑，更數政未得償，官罷不能去。

translations.literal: A county clerk had depleted the treasury funds; through several administrations it had not been repaid, and when dismissed from office he could not leave.
translations.idiomatic: A county clerk had embezzled treasury funds, and through several successive administrations the debt had never been cleared; when he was removed from office he could not leave until it was paid.

sentences.zh: 興祚至，為請豁除，其當償者出私財代輸。

translations.literal: When Xingzuo arrived, he petitioned for remission of what could be waived; for what should be repaid he paid out of private funds in substitution.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingzuo took office, he obtained remission of what could be forgiven, and paid what remained from his own purse.

sentences.zh: 清丈通縣田，編號繪圖，因田徵賦。

translations.literal: He surveyed and measured the fields throughout the county, assigned numbers and drew maps, and levied taxes according to the fields.
translations.idiomatic: He conducted a county-wide land survey, registered and mapped every field, and assessed taxes accordingly.

sentences.zh: 飛詭隱匿，皆不得行。

translations.literal: Contrivances to evade and conceal could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: No evasion or concealment could get past him.

sentences.zh: 縣徭役未均，最煩苦者為圖六。

translations.literal: The corvée labor throughout the county was not evenly distributed; the most onerous fell on Map Six.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée duties in the county were unevenly distributed, and Map Six bore the heaviest burden.

sentences.zh: 興祚以入官田徵租僱役，民害乃除。

translations.literal: Xingzuo used official income lands to collect rent and hire labor for service; the people's suffering was then removed.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzuo funded the corvée by collecting rent from government-held lands and hiring substitutes, lifting the burden from the people.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，為粥食餓者。

translations.literal: In a year of famine, he prepared porridge to feed the hungry.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year he set up soup kitchens for the starving.

sentences.zh: 八旗兵駐防蘇州，興祚請於領兵固山，單騎彈壓。

translations.literal: The Eight Banner troops were garrisoned at Suzhou; Xingzuo requested of the garrison commander the banner general, and alone on horseback suppressed unrest.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eight Banner troops were garrisoned at Suzhou, Xingzuo asked leave of their banner commander to ride out alone and restore order.

sentences.zh: 兵或取民雞，立笞之，皆奉約束。

translations.literal: When soldiers sometimes took the people's chickens, he immediately had them flogged; all then observed discipline.
translations.idiomatic: When soldiers stole chickens from the locals he had them flogged on the spot, and thereafter they kept to the rules.

sentences.zh: 塘溢，兵不得渡，立竹於塘旁，懸燈以為識，騎行如坦途。

translations.literal: A pond overflowed and the soldiers could not cross; he set up bamboo poles beside the pond and hung lamps as markers, and riding proceeded as on level ground.
translations.idiomatic: When a pond flooded and blocked the soldiers' passage, he planted bamboo stakes along its edge and hung lanterns to mark the way, so they could ride across as if on open road.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，遷行人，仍留知縣事，用漕運總督帥顏保薦，超擢福建按察使。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi he was transferred to the post of Courier, but still retained magisterial duties; on recommendation of Grain Transport Governor Shuai Yanbao he was abruptly promoted to Fujian Surveillance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi he was transferred to the Board of Couriers but kept his magisterial duties; on the recommendation of Grain Transport Governor Shuai Yanbao he was promoted straight to Fujian Surveillance Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 有朱統錩者，號明裔，耿精忠私署敉遠將軍，及精忠降，自稱宜春王，據貴溪為亂，與福建錯壤。

translations.literal: There was one Zhu Tongqian, who styled himself a Ming descendant; Geng Jingzhong had privately appointed him Pacification General of the Far Reaches, and when Jingzhong surrendered he proclaimed himself Prince of Yichun, seized Guixi in rebellion, and his territory bordered Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: One Zhu Tongqian claimed descent from the Ming; Geng Jingzhong had made him Pacification General of the Far Reaches, and after Jingzhong's surrender he styled himself Prince of Yichun, raised rebellion from Guixi, and his territory marched with Fujian.

sentences.zh: 興祚輕騎至光澤，撫其將陳龍等，遣降將陽自歸為內應，令龍導師入，其將馮珩等縛統錩，率兵三千以降。

translations.literal: Xingzuo with a light escort went to Guangze, reassured their general Chen Long and others, sent the surrendered general Yang Zigui as inside response, had Long guide the army in, and his generals Feng Heng and others bound Tongqian and led three thousand troops to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzuo rode to Guangze with a small force, won over the rebel general Chen Long, and sent the surrendered officer Yang Zigui as an inside agent; Chen Long guided the government troops in, Feng Heng and others seized Zhu Tongqian, and three thousand men surrendered.

sentences.zh: 十七年，擢巡撫。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was appointed provincial governor.

sentences.zh: 時鄭錦踞台灣，遣其驍將劉國軒等陷漳、泉屬縣，复圍泉州。

translations.literal: At that time Zheng Jing held Taiwan, sent his fierce general Liu Guoxuan and others to seize counties subordinate to Zhang and Quan, and again besieged Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jing held Taiwan and sent his crack general Liu Guoxuan to overrun the counties around Zhangzhou and Quanzhou, then laid siege to Quanzhou once more.

sentences.zh: 興祚率標兵自興化赴援，至仙遊，錦將黃球等率二千人結土寇萬餘屯白鴿嶺。

translations.literal: Xingzuo led the banner troops from Xinghua to the relief, and at Xianyou, Jing's general Huang Qiu and others led two thousand men and joined more than ten thousand local bandits to encamp at Baige Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzuo led his banner troops from Xinghua to relieve the city; at Xianyou, Zheng Jing's general Huang Qiu mustered two thousand men and joined forces with more than ten thousand local rebels at Baige Ridge.

sentences.zh: 興祚分兵三道，自當中路，與戰，自辰至酉，相持不即退。

translations.literal: Xingzuo divided his force into three routes, himself taking the center, fought with them from the chen hour to the you hour, and the two sides held without either side immediately retreating.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzuo divided his army into three columns and took the center himself; the battle raged from morning till evening without either side giving ground.

sentences.zh: 興祚遣兵自間道奪白鴿嶺關口，斬級六百，墮岸溺水死者甚眾，寇乃潰走，追敗之於嶺頭灣，复永春、德化二縣。

translations.literal: Xingzuo sent troops by a bypath to seize the pass at Baige Ridge, beheaded six hundred, and very many fell from the banks and drowned; the bandits then broke and fled, and he pursued and defeated them at Lingtou Bay, recovering the two counties of Yongchun and Dehua.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzuo sent troops by a hidden path to seize the pass at Baige Ridge, killing six hundred enemies and drowning many more as they fled over the banks; the rebels broke and ran, and he chased them down at Lingtou Bay and retook Yongchun and Dehua.

sentences.zh: 國軒自泉州走入海，以巨艦數百出沒赤嶼、黃崎諸處。

translations.literal: Guoxuan fled from Quanzhou into the sea, and with several hundred great warships appeared and vanished at Chiyu, Huangqi, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxuan escaped from Quanzhou by sea and prowled the waters off Chiyu, Huangqi, and nearby islands with several hundred large warships.

sentences.zh: 興祚遣總兵林賢等統水師出海，分三路夾攻，焚敵艦六十餘，俘斬六千有奇。

translations.literal: Xingzuo sent Regional Commander Lin Xian and others to command the naval forces out to sea, divided into three routes for converging attack, burned more than sixty enemy ships, and captured and beheaded somewhat more than six thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzuo sent Regional Commander Lin Xian and the fleet to sea in three columns; they burned more than sixty enemy vessels and killed or captured some six thousand men.

sentences.zh: 疏報捷，並言：「海逆逼犯漳、泉，大軍由陸路進發，跋涉疲難。

translations.literal: In his memorial reporting victory he also said: 'The sea rebels press upon Zhang and Quan; the great army advances by land route, and the toilsome march is arduous.'
translations.idiomatic: In his victory report he added: "The rebels at sea are pressing hard on Zhangzhou and Quanzhou; overland marches are exhausting and slow.

sentences.zh: 臣前捐募水兵，一戰破賊，但兵力稍薄，未易輕取廈門。

translations.literal: Your servant previously donated funds to recruit naval soldiers, and in one battle broke the bandits, but the military strength is somewhat thin and it is not easy lightly to take Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: I have already raised naval troops at my own expense and broke the enemy in one engagement, but our forces are still too few to take Xiamen lightly.

sentences.zh: 若得水師二萬，再添造戰船，可直搗巢穴，掃蕩鯨波。

translations.literal: If one obtains twenty thousand naval troops and additionally builds war vessels, one can straightway strike their nest and sweep the whale waves.
translations.idiomatic: With twenty thousand sailors and a fresh fleet of warships, we could strike their stronghold directly and clear the seas.

sentences.zh: 」詔允行。

translations.literal: ' An edict approved and ordered implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 十八年，國軒率兵二千至郭塘、歐溪頭，欲斷江東橋以犯長泰，興祚與都統吉勒塔布、總督姚啟聖會師擊走之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Guoxuan led two thousand troops to Guotang and Ouxitou, intending to cut Jiangdong Bridge to invade Changtai; Xingzuo, together with Commandant Jiletabu and Governor Qisheng, joined forces and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Guoxuan marched two thousand men to Guotang and Ouxitou, planning to sever Jiangdong Bridge and attack Changtai; Xingzuo joined Commandant Jiletabu and Governor Yao Qisheng and drove him back.

sentences.zh: 興祚遣驛傳道王國泰等招降錦將蔡衝琱、林忠等三百八十五人，兵萬二千五百，拔難民千二百，得舟六十七。

translations.literal: Xingzuo sent couriers along the post roads, with Wang Guotai and others, to induce the surrender of Jing's generals Cai Chongdiao, Lin Zhong, and three hundred eighty-five others, twelve thousand five hundred troops, rescued one thousand two hundred refugees, and obtained sixty-seven boats.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzuo sent Wang Guotai and other envoys along the post roads to win over Zheng Jing's generals Cai Chongdiao, Lin Zhong, and 385 others, along with 12,500 soldiers; they rescued 1,200 civilians and captured sixty-seven boats.

sentences.zh: 敘前後功，進秩正一品。

translations.literal: In recording his earlier and later merit, his rank was advanced to the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: For his accumulated services he was raised to the first rank.

sentences.zh: 十九年，疏言：「鄭錦盤踞廈門，沿海生靈受其荼毒。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he submitted a memorial saying: 'Zheng Jing occupies Xiamen, and the living souls along the coast suffer his torment.'
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he memorialized: "Zheng Jing holds Xiamen, and the coastal population has long endured his depredations.

sentences.zh: 臣去冬新造戰船，水師提督萬正色分配將士，自閩安出大洋操練。

translations.literal: Your servant last winter newly built war vessels; Naval Commissioner Wan Zhengse assigned officers and troops, and from Min'an went out into the great ocean for drills.
translations.idiomatic: Last winter I had new warships built; Naval Commissioner Wan Zhengse has assigned officers and men and is drilling them in the open sea off Min'an.

sentences.zh: 俟舊存船艘修葺完整，江南砲手齊集，即相機進取廈門。

translations.literal: When the ships previously on hand are repaired and made complete, and Jiangnan gunners all assemble, then according to opportunity advance to take Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: Once the older vessels are fully repaired and the Jiangnan gunners are assembled, we shall seize the moment and take Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 」二月，正色師進海壇，興祚自泉州會寧海將軍拉哈達、總兵王英等赴同安，攻克汭洲、潯尾諸隘。

translations.literal: ' In the second month Zhengse's army advanced to Haitan; Xingzuo from Quanzhou joined Ninghai General Lahada, Regional Commander Wang Ying, and others and went to Tong'an, capturing the passes at Ruizhou, Xunwei, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Wan Zhengse advanced on Haitan; Xingzuo left Quanzhou to join Ninghai General Lahada, Regional Commander Wang Ying, and others at Tong'an, and they stormed the passes at Ruizhou, Xunwei, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 渡海，拉哈達出中路，英右，興祚左，奮戰，敵大潰，遂克廈門。

translations.literal: Crossing the sea, Lahada went out on the center route, Ying on the right, Xingzuo on the left; they fought fiercely, the enemy greatly broke, and thus Xiamen was taken.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed the strait with Lahada in the center, Wang Ying on the right, and Xingzuo on the left; after a hard fight the enemy collapsed and Xiamen fell.

sentences.zh: 時正色已取海壇，降錦將朱天貴等，復遣兵取金門，餘眾悉竄台灣。

translations.literal: At that time Zhengse had already taken Haitan and induced Jing's general Zhu Tiangui and others to surrender; he again sent troops to take Jinmen, and the remaining masses all fled to Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Zhengse had already taken Haitan and accepted the surrender of Zheng Jing's general Zhu Tiangui; government troops then seized Jinmen, and the remaining rebels fled to Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，詔嘉獎，下部優敘。

translations.literal: When the victory was reported, an edict praised and rewarded him, and the ministry was ordered to record merit favorably.
translations.idiomatic: On news of the victory the emperor issued commendations and ordered the ministries to register the merits of all involved.

sentences.zh: 興祚因請留澳民防守，蠲荒田租糧，減關課。

translations.literal: Xingzuo thereupon requested to retain harbor-dwelling people for defense, remit rent grain on wasteland fields, and reduce pass duties.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzuo asked to keep local harbor communities for garrison duty, waive grain rents on abandoned fields, and cut customs levies.

sentences.zh: 正色亦請於海澄、廈門分兵駐守。

translations.literal: Zhengse also requested to divide troops for garrison at Haicheng and Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Zhengse also asked to station garrisons at Haicheng and Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 上命侍郎溫岱赴福建會議。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Vice Minister Wen Dai to go to Fujian for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Vice Minister Wen Dai to Fujian to investigate.

sentences.zh: 溫岱至，啟聖與言正色复海壇，與天貴先有約乃進兵，無殺賊攻克事。

translations.literal: When Wen Dai arrived, Qisheng told him that Zhengse recovered Haitan only because he had an earlier agreement with Tiangui before advancing troops; there was no matter of killing bandits to capture it.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Dai arrived, Yao Qisheng told him that Wan Zhengse had retaken Haitan only because he had struck a deal with Zhu Tiangui beforehand—that no real fighting had been involved.

sentences.zh: 溫岱還京師，兵部據其言，議興祚冒功，上命仍議敘，予世職拜他喇布勒哈番兼拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: Wen Dai returned to the capital; the Board of War based on his words deliberated that Xingzuo had falsely claimed merit; the emperor ordered merit still to be recorded, and granted hereditary office of combined Tabuleha-fun and Tuosalahafun.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Dai reported to the capital; on his testimony the Board of War questioned whether Xingzuo had inflated his claims, but the emperor ordered his merits recorded nonetheless and granted him the combined hereditary ranks of Tabuleha-fun and Tuosalahafun.

sentences.zh: 二十年，擢兩廣總督。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was promoted to Governor-General of the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was appointed governor-general of the Two Guangs.

sentences.zh: 興祚上官，疏言尚之信在廣東橫徵苛斂，民受其害數十年。

translations.literal: When Xingzuo took up his post, he submitted a memorial saying that Shang Zhixin in Guangdong levied arbitrarily and collected harshly, and the people had suffered harm for decades.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office, Xingzuo memorialized that Shang Zhixin had for decades imposed arbitrary levies and extortionate taxes on Guangdong, to the people's grievous harm.

sentences.zh: 因舉鹽埠、渡稅、稅總店、漁課諸害，悉奏罷之。

translations.literal: Thereupon citing such abuses as salt wharves, ferry taxes, tax general stores, and fishery levies, he memorialized to abolish them all.
translations.idiomatic: He enumerated abuses including salt monopolies, ferry tolls, tax brokers, and fishing levies, and had them all abolished.

sentences.zh: 自遷界令下，廣東沿海居民多失業，興祚疏請展界，恣民捕採耕種。

translations.literal: Since the relocation-boundary edict was issued, many coastal residents of Guangdong lost their livelihoods; Xingzuo submitted a memorial requesting extension of the boundary, allowing the people freely to fish, gather, and cultivate.
translations.idiomatic: After the coastal evacuation order, many Guangdong fishermen and farmers lost their livelihoods; Xingzuo asked to roll back the boundary so people could return to fishing, foraging, and farming.

sentences.zh: 上遣尚書杜臻、內閣學士石柱會興祚巡歷規畫，兵民皆得所。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Minister Du Zhen and Grand Secretariat Academician Shi Zhu to join Xingzuo in touring and planning; soldiers and people all obtained their proper places.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched Minister Du Zhen and Grand Secretariat Academician Shi Zhu to tour the coast with Xingzuo and lay out new boundaries; both garrison and civilians found their places again.

sentences.zh: 又言潮州海汛遼闊，商民往來貿易，恐宵小潛踪，應令澄海協達濠營水汛官兵船隻改歸南澳水師鎮統轄，與碣石鎮互相聯絡，巡防外海島嶼，詔並允行。

translations.literal: He also said that the Chaozhou sea patrol area was vast and wide; merchants and people came and went in trade, and one feared petty men might lurk hidden; it should be ordered that the naval patrol officers, troops, and vessels of Chenghai Assistant Commandant Dadao Fort garrison be transferred to the jurisdiction of the Nan'ao Naval Garrison, linking with Jieshi Garrison in mutual contact, to patrol and guard outer-sea islands; an edict approved all and ordered implementation.
translations.idiomatic: He also noted that Chaozhou's coastal waters were vast and that bandits might hide among trading traffic; he proposed transferring the naval patrol from Chenghai's Dadao Fort to Nan'ao Naval Command and coordinating with Jieshi Garrison to patrol the offshore islands. The emperor approved all these measures.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，疏請於廣東、廣西二省設爐鼓鑄，給事中錢晉錫、御史王君詔疏劾興祚鼓鑄浮冒，下吏議，當鐫秩，命以副都統用。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he memorialized requesting the establishment of furnace coin-casting in the two provinces of Guangdong and Guangxi. Supervising Secretary Qian Jinxi and Censor Wang Junzhao memorialized impeaching Xingzuo for inflated coin-casting; the case was sent down for official deliberation, the penalty being demotion by stripping rank, but he was ordered to serve as vice commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he asked to set up mints in Guangdong and Guangxi. Supervising Secretary Qian Jinxi and Censor Wang Junzhao accused him of padding the coin-casting accounts; after review he was found liable for demotion, but was allowed to remain in service as a vice commandant.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，授歸化城右翼漢軍副都統，复坐事鐫秩。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he was appointed vice commandant of the Right Wing Han Army at Guihuacheng; again, because of an offense, his rank was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he was made vice commandant of the Right Wing Han Army at Guihuacheng, but was again demoted after an offense.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，上徵噶爾丹，命自呼坦和碩至寧夏安十三塘，興祚原效力坐沙克舒爾塘，未幾，復原秩。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, when the emperor campaigned against Galdan, he ordered thirteen supply depots established from Hutankeshuo to Ningxia. Xingzuo had originally volunteered for service and was posted at Shakshurtang Depot; before long his original rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year, during the campaign against Galdan, the court ordered thirteen supply stations set up from Hutankeshuo to Ningxia. Xingzuo, who had volunteered for duty at Shakshurtang, soon had his former rank restored.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirty-sixth year.

sentences.zh: 興祚為政持大體，除煩苛，卒後遠近戴之。

translations.literal: In governing, Xingzuo upheld broad principles and removed troublesome exactions; after his death, people near and far revered him.
translations.idiomatic: As an administrator Xingzuo kept to the larger principles of government and cleared away petty harshness; after his death he was honored far and near.

sentences.zh: 歷官之地，並籥祀名宦。

translations.literal: In every place where he had served, he was all entered into enshrinement among distinguished officials.
translations.idiomatic: In every jurisdiction where he had served, he was entered into the shrine of distinguished officials.

sentences.zh: =施琅=施琅，字琢公，福建晉江人。

translations.literal: Shi Lang, style name Zhuogong, was a native of Jinjiang in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Lang, whose style was Zhuogong, came from Jinjiang in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 初為明總兵鄭芝龍部下左衝鋒。

translations.literal: At first he was left vanguard under Ming regional commander Zheng Zhilong.
translations.idiomatic: He began as left vanguard under the Ming regional commander Zheng Zhilong.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，師定福建，瑯從芝龍降。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi, when the armies pacified Fujian, Lang followed Zhilong in surrendering.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shunzhi, when the Qing armies pacified Fujian, Lang surrendered with Zhilong.

sentences.zh: 從征廣東，戡定順德、東莞、三水、新寧諸縣。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign into Guangdong and pacified the counties of Shunde, Dongguan, Sanshui, and Xinning.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Guangdong campaign and pacified Shunde, Dongguan, Sanshui, Xinning, and the other counties.

sentences.zh: 芝龍歸京師，其子成功竄踞海島，招瑯，不從。

translations.literal: Zhilong returned to the capital; his son Chenggong fled to hold an island and recruited Lang, but Lang did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhilong went to the capital, his son Chenggong seized an island and summoned Lang, but Lang refused.

sentences.zh: 成功執瑯，並縶其家屬。

translations.literal: Chenggong seized Lang and also imprisoned his family members.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong arrested Lang and imprisoned his family as well.

sentences.zh: 瑯以計得脫，父大宣、弟顯及子侄皆為成功所殺。

translations.literal: Lang escaped by stratagem; his father Daxuan, his brother Xian, and his sons and nephews were all killed by Chenggong.
translations.idiomatic: Lang escaped by a ruse, but Chenggong killed his father Daxuan, his brother Xian, and his sons and nephews.

sentences.zh: 十三年，從定遠大將軍世子濟度擊敗成功於福州，授同安副將。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he followed the Prince Heir of the Far-Pacifying Grand General Jidu in defeating Chenggong at Fuzhou and was appointed vice commander of Tong'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he served under Prince Jidu, heir of the Far-Pacifying Grand General, in defeating Chenggong at Fuzhou and was made vice commander of Tong'an.

sentences.zh: 十六年，成功據台灣，就擢瑯同安總兵。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Chenggong held Taiwan; Lang was thereupon promoted to regional commander of Tong'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, with Chenggong holding Taiwan, Lang was promoted to regional commander of Tong'an.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，遷水師提督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi he was transferred to naval commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kangxi he became naval commander.

sentences.zh: 時成功已死，其子錦率眾欲犯海澄，瑯遣守備汪明等率舟師御之海門，斬其將林維，獲戰船、軍械。

translations.literal: At that time Chenggong was already dead; his son Jing led a host intending to invade Haicheng. Lang sent Garrison Commander Wang Ming and others to lead the fleet to meet them at Haimen, beheaded their general Lin Wei, and captured war vessels and military equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong was already dead, and his son Jing led a force against Haicheng. Lang sent Garrison Commander Wang Ming and others with the fleet to meet them at Haimen, killed their general Lin Wei, and seized warships and arms.

sentences.zh: 未幾，靖南王耿繼茂、總督李率泰等攻克廈門，敵驚潰，瑯募荷蘭國水兵，以夾板船要擊，斬級千餘，乘勝取浯嶼、金門二島。

translations.literal: Before long Prince Jingnan Geng Jimao, Governor Li Shuaitai, and others captured Xiamen; the enemy fled in panic and collapse. Lang recruited Dutch naval soldiers and with double-hulled ships intercepted them, took more than a thousand heads, and following up the victory seized the two islands of Wuyu and Jinmen.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Prince Jingnan Geng Jimao, Governor Li Shuaitai, and others took Xiamen; the enemy broke and fled. Lang hired Dutch sailors, intercepted them with double-hulled warships, killed more than a thousand men, and pressed on to seize Wuyu and Jinmen.

sentences.zh: 敘功，加右都督。

translations.literal: In recording merit he was promoted to Right Commandant-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: For his services he was given the rank of Right Commandant-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 三年，加靖海將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year he was given the additional title Pacifying-the-Seas General.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made Pacifying-the-Seas General.

sentences.zh: 七年，瑯密陳錦負嵎海上，宜急攻之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Lang confidentially memorialized that Jing, defiant on the sea, should be attacked urgently.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Lang secretly urged that Jing, clinging defiantly to the sea, should be attacked at once.

sentences.zh: 召詣京師，上詢方略，瑯言：「賊兵不滿數万，戰船不過數百，錦智勇俱無。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the capital; the emperor inquired about strategy. Lang said: "The rebels' troops number fewer than ten thousand; their warships are no more than several hundred. Jing lacks both wit and courage.
translations.idiomatic: He was called to the capital, and when the emperor asked his plan Lang replied: "The rebels have fewer than ten thousand men and no more than a few hundred warships. Jing has neither wit nor courage.

sentences.zh: 若先取澎湖以扼其吭，賊勢立絀；

translations.literal: If we first take Penghu to choke their vital point, rebel strength will immediately weaken;"
translations.idiomatic: If we take Penghu first and choke off their lifeline, the rebels will weaken at once;"

sentences.zh: 倘复負固，則重師泊台灣港口，而別以奇兵分襲南路打狗港及北路文​​港海翁堀。

translations.literal: If they again hold firm, then mass troops at Taiwan's harbor while separately sending surprise forces to raid in division the southern route at Takao Harbor and the northern route at Wengang and Haiweng Qu.
translations.idiomatic: If they still resist, anchor the main force in Taiwan's harbors and send separate strike columns against Takao on the south and Wengang and Haiweng Qu on the north.

sentences.zh: 賊分則力薄，合則勢蹙，台灣計日可平。

translations.literal: If the rebels divide their forces they will be thin; if they unite, their situation will be tight; Taiwan can be pacified within days."
translations.idiomatic: If they split their forces they will be too thin to hold; if they mass together they will be cornered. Taiwan can be taken in a matter of days."

sentences.zh: 」事下部議，寢其奏。

translations.literal: The matter was sent to the ministries for deliberation, and his memorial was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was referred to the ministries for discussion and then shelved.

sentences.zh: 因裁水師提督，授瑯內大臣，隸鑲黃旗漢軍。

translations.literal: Accordingly the post of naval commander was abolished; Lang was appointed grand minister of the Inner Court and attached to the Han Army of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: The naval command was abolished, and Lang was made a grand minister of the Inner Court under the Han Army of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 二十年，錦死，子克塽幼，諸將劉國軒、馮錫範用事。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Jing died; his son Keshuang was young; the generals Liu Guoxuan and Feng Xifan wielded power.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year Jing died, leaving his young son Keshuang; the generals Liu Guoxuan and Feng Xifan held the reins of power.

sentences.zh: 內閣學士李光地奏台灣可取狀，因薦​​瑯習海上事，上复授瑯福建水師提督，加太子少保，諭相機進取。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Li Guangdi memorialized on the condition in which Taiwan could be taken and recommended Lang as experienced in maritime affairs. The emperor again appointed Lang Fujian naval commander, added the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and instructed him to seize the opportune moment to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Li Guangdi reported that Taiwan could be taken and recommended Lang for his mastery of sea warfare. The emperor restored him as Fujian naval commander, made him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and told him to strike when the moment was right.

sentences.zh: 瑯至軍，疏言：「賊船久泊澎湖，悉力固守。

translations.literal: When Lang reached the army, he memorialized: "The rebels' ships have long been anchored at Penghu, defending with all their strength.
translations.idiomatic: When Lang joined the army he wrote: "The rebel fleet has long been stationed at Penghu and is holding the islands with all its strength.

sentences.zh: 冬春之際，颶風時發，我舟驟難過洋。

translations.literal: Between winter and spring, hurricanes often arise, and our vessels cannot readily cross the open sea.
translations.idiomatic: Between winter and spring hurricanes strike often, and our ships cannot easily make the crossing.

sentences.zh: 臣今練習水師，又遣間諜通臣舊時部曲，使為內應。

translations.literal: Your servant is now drilling the fleet and also sending spies to contact my former subordinates, to serve as internal collaborators.
translations.idiomatic: I am now training the fleet and sending agents to my old followers to arrange inside help.

sentences.zh: 俟風便，可獲全勝。

translations.literal: Awaiting favorable winds, we can win a complete victory."
translations.idiomatic: When the winds turn favorable, we can win a complete victory."

sentences.zh: 」二十一年，給事中孫蕙疏言宜緩徵台灣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Supervising Secretary Sun Hui memorialized that the conquest of Taiwan should be deferred.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year Supervising Secretary Sun Hui argued that the Taiwan campaign should be postponed.

sentences.zh: 七月，彗星見，戶部尚書梁清標復以為言，詔暫緩進剿。

translations.literal: In the seventh month a comet appeared; Minister of Revenue Liang Qingbiao again spoke on the matter, and an edict temporarily deferred the advance against the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month a comet appeared; Minister of Revenue Liang Qingbiao raised the matter again, and the court ordered the expedition deferred for the time being.

sentences.zh: 瑯疏言：「臣已簡水師精兵二萬、戰船三百，足破滅海賊。

translations.literal: Lang memorialized: "Your servant has already selected twenty thousand picked naval troops and three hundred warships, enough to destroy the sea rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Lang replied: "I have already chosen twenty thousand elite sailors and three hundred warships, enough to destroy the pirates at sea.

sentences.zh: 請趣督撫治糧餉，但遇風利，即可進行，並請調陸路官兵協剿。

translations.literal: I request that the governor and provincial commissioner be urged to prepare provisions and pay; once the winds are favorable, we can advance at once, and I also ask that land troops and officers be transferred to assist in the campaign."
translations.idiomatic: Urge the governor-general and provincial officials to ready supplies and rations; as soon as the winds serve we can sail, and please assign land forces to join the attack."

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 二十二年六月，瑯自桐山攻克花嶼、貓嶼、草嶼，乘南風進泊八罩。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-second year Lang himself advanced from Tongshan, captured Huayu, Maoyu, and Caoyu, and riding the south wind moved forward to anchor at Bazhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twenty-second year Lang sailed from Tongshan, took Huayu, Maoyu, and Caoyu, and rode the south wind to anchor at Bazhao.

sentences.zh: 國軒踞澎湖，緣岸築短牆，置腰銃，環二十餘里為壁壘。

translations.literal: Guoxuan held Penghu, built short walls along the shore, placed waist guns, and encircled more than twenty li as a fortified line.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxuan held Penghu, threw up low walls along the shore, mounted swivel guns, and ringed more than twenty li of coast with fortifications.

sentences.zh: 瑯遣游擊藍理以鳥船進攻，敵舟乘潮四合。

translations.literal: Lang sent Raiding Officer Lan Li to advance with bird ships; enemy vessels joined from four directions on the tide.
translations.idiomatic: Lang sent Raiding Officer Lan Li against them in light warships; the enemy ships closed in from every side on the rising tide.

sentences.zh: 瑯乘樓船突入賊陣，流矢傷目，血溢於帕，督戰不少卻，總兵吳英繼之，斬級三千，克虎井、桶盤二嶼。

translations.literal: Lang rode a tower ship and burst into the rebel formation; a stray arrow wounded his eye, blood overflowing his headcloth, yet he directed the battle without the slightest retreat. Regional Commander Wu Ying followed; more than three thousand heads were taken, and Tiger Well and Tongpan, the two islets, were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Lang drove a tower ship into the enemy line; a stray arrow struck his eye and blood soaked his headcloth, but he never slackened command. Regional Commander Wu Ying pressed the attack, three thousand heads were taken, and the islets of Hujing and Tongpan were seized.

sentences.zh: 旋以百船分列東西，遣總兵陳蟒、魏明、董義、康玉率兵東指雞籠峪、四角山，西指牛心灣，分賊勢。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, with a hundred ships arrayed east and west, he sent regional commanders Chen Mang, Wei Ming, Dong Yi, and Kang Yu to lead troops east toward Jilong Yu and Sijiao Mountain and west toward Niuxin Bay, dividing rebel strength.
translations.idiomatic: He then split a hundred ships east and west, sending regional commanders Chen Mang, Wei Ming, Dong Yi, and Kang Yu east toward Jilong Yu and Sijiao Mountain and west toward Niuxin Bay to divide the enemy force.

sentences.zh: 瑯自督五十六船分八隊，以八十船繼後，揚帆直進。

translations.literal: Lang personally directed fifty-six ships in eight squadrons, with eighty ships following behind, and sailed straight forward.
translations.idiomatic: Lang himself led fifty-six ships in eight squadrons, with eighty more following, and drove straight ahead under full sail.

sentences.zh: 敵悉眾拒戰，總兵林賢、朱天貴先入陣，天貴戰死。

translations.literal: The enemy mustered all their forces to resist; regional commanders Lin Xian and Zhu Tiangui entered the formation first, and Tiangui died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy massed every man to resist; regional commanders Lin Xian and Zhu Tiangui led the charge, and Tiangui fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 將士奮勇衷擊，自辰至申，焚敵艦百餘，溺死無算，遂取澎湖，國軒遁歸台灣​​。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers fought fiercely in concert; from the hour chen to the hour shen they burned more than a hundred enemy ships and drowned countless men, then took Penghu, and Guoxuan fled back to Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: The men fought with desperate fury from mid-morning until late afternoon, burning more than a hundred enemy ships and drowning untold numbers; Penghu fell, and Guoxuan fled back to Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 克塽大驚，遣使詣軍前乞降，瑯疏陳，上許之。

translations.literal: Keshuang was greatly alarmed, sent envoys to the army to beg surrender; Lang memorialized the situation, and the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Keshuang was terrified and sent envoys to the camp to sue for peace; Lang reported this, and the emperor accepted.

sentences.zh: 八月，瑯統兵入鹿耳門，至台灣。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Lang led his troops through Lukang and arrived in Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Lang led his army through Lukang into Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 克塽率屬薙發，迎於水次，繳延平王金印。

translations.literal: Keshuang led his followers in shaving their heads and met him at the water's edge, surrendering the golden seal of the Prince of Yanping.
translations.idiomatic: Keshuang came with his followers, heads shaven in submission, to meet Lang at the shore and handed over the golden seal of the Prince of Yanping.

sentences.zh: 台灣平，自海道報捷。

translations.literal: Taiwan was pacified, and victory was reported by the sea route.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwan was pacified, and word of victory was sent home by sea.

sentences.zh: 疏至，正中秋，上賦詩旌瑯功，复授靖海將軍，封靖海侯，世襲罔替，賜御用袍及諸服物。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, it was exactly Mid-Autumn; the emperor composed a poem to extol Lang's merit, again appointed him Pacifying the Seas General, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Pacifying the Seas with perpetual hereditary succession, and granted imperial robes and various garments.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial arrived at the height of Mid-Autumn Festival. The emperor composed a poem to honor Lang's achievements, again appointed him Pacifying the Seas General, created him Marquis of Pacifying the Seas with perpetual hereditary rank, and bestowed imperial robes and other gifts of apparel.

sentences.zh: 瑯疏辭侯封，乞得如內大臣例賜花翎，部議謂非例，上命毋辭，並如其請賜花翎。

translations.literal: Lang memorialized declining the marquisate, begging to receive a peacock feather by the precedent of Inner Ministers; the Board deliberated that it was not precedented; the emperor ordered him not to decline, and also granted a peacock feather as he requested.
translations.idiomatic: Lang asked to be allowed to refuse the marquisate and instead receive a peacock feather, as was granted to Inner Ministers. The Board argued that this was without precedent, but the emperor told him to accept the enfeoffment and also granted the peacock feather as he had asked.

sentences.zh: 遣侍郎蘇拜至福建，與督撫及瑯議善後事。

translations.literal: A vice minister, Subai, was dispatched to Fujian to discuss postwar arrangements with the governors and Lang.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Vice Minister Subai to Fujian to work with the provincial governors and Lang on settling affairs after the campaign.

sentences.zh: 有言宜遷其人、棄其地者，瑯疏言：「明季設澎水標於金門，出汛至澎湖而止。

translations.literal: Some said the people ought to be relocated and the land abandoned. Lang memorialized, saying: "In the late Ming the Penghu Water Fleet was established at Kinmen; patrols went out only as far as Penghu.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued that Taiwan's people should be moved off the island and the territory abandoned. Lang replied in a memorial: "In the late Ming a Penghu patrol fleet was stationed at Kinmen, and its patrols extended no farther than Penghu.

sentences.zh: 台灣原屬化外，土番雜處，未入版圖。

translations.literal: Taiwan originally belonged outside civilization, with indigenous tribes intermingled, and had not entered the official maps.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwan had lain beyond the frontier, with indigenous peoples living among one another, and had never been counted within the empire's maps.

sentences.zh: 然其時中國之民潛往生聚，已不下萬人。

translations.literal: Yet at that time Chinese people secretly went there to gather and settle, numbering no less than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, Chinese settlers had already gone there in secret, and their numbers were no fewer than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 鄭芝龍為海寇，據為巢穴。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhilong was a sea bandit and took it as his lair.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhilong, a pirate of the seas, made it his stronghold.

sentences.zh: 及崇禎元年，芝龍就撫，借與紅毛為互市之所。

translations.literal: By the first year of Chongzhen, Zhilong submitted to pacification and lent it to the Red-haired as a place for mutual trade.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongzhen, Zhilong accepted government pacification and leased it to the Dutch as a trading station.
