sentences.zh: 紅毛聯結土番，招納內地民，漸作邊患。

translations.literal: The Red-haired allied with indigenous tribes, recruited inland people, and gradually became a frontier threat.
translations.idiomatic: The Dutch allied with the indigenous tribes, drew in people from the interior, and slowly became a threat along the frontier.

sentences.zh: 至順治十八年，鄭成功盤踞其地，糾集亡命，荼毒海疆。

translations.literal: By the eighteenth year of Shunzhi, Zheng Chenggong entrenched himself there, mustered fugitive desperadoes, and plagued the maritime frontier.
translations.idiomatic: By the eighteenth year of Shunzhi, Zheng Chenggong had seized the island, gathering fugitives and outlaws and ravaging the coast.

sentences.zh: 傳及其孫克塽，積數十年。

translations.literal: The succession passed to his grandson Keshuang, accumulating several decades.
translations.idiomatic: Power passed down to his grandson Keshuang, and this continued for decades.

sentences.zh: 一旦納土歸命，善後之計，尤宜周詳。

translations.literal: Now that they have suddenly surrendered territory and submitted to command, plans for the aftermath ought especially to be thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Now that they have surrendered the land and submitted in a single stroke, the plans for what follows must be worked out with especial care.

sentences.zh: 若棄其地、遷其人，以有限之船，渡無限之民，非閱數年，難以報竣。

translations.literal: If the land were abandoned and the people relocated, using limited ships to ferry unlimited people, without several years it would be hard to report completion.
translations.idiomatic: To abandon the territory and move the population would mean carrying an unlimited number of people on a limited fleet of ships—a task that could hardly be finished in fewer than several years.

sentences.zh: 倘渡載不盡，竄匿山谷，所謂藉寇兵而齎盜糧也。

translations.literal: If ferrying could not carry them all, those hiding in mountain valleys would be, as the saying goes, lending arms to bandits and carrying grain for thieves.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who could not be shipped off would hide in the hills—giving bandits weapons and provisions, as the old saying has it.

sentences.zh: 且此地原為紅毛所有，乘隙复踞，必竊窺內地，鼓惑人心。

translations.literal: Moreover this land originally belonged to the Red-haired; if they seized the opening to reoccupy it, they would surely covertly watch the interior and stir up men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, this island once belonged to the Dutch. If they seized the chance to reoccupy it, they would surely spy on the interior provinces and sow unrest among the people.

sentences.zh: 重以夾板船之精堅，海外無敵，沿海諸省，斷難安然無虞。

translations.literal: Added to this, their double-hulled ships are finely built and unmatched overseas; the coastal provinces could hardly remain secure and untroubled.
translations.idiomatic: With their double-hulled warships, stoutly built and unmatched on the seas, the coastal provinces could scarcely remain safe.

sentences.zh: 至時復勤師遠征，恐未易見效。

translations.literal: When the time came to mobilize troops again for a distant campaign, success would likely not come easily.
translations.idiomatic: When the court had to send armies on another distant expedition, victory would not come easily.

sentences.zh: 如僅守澎湖，則孤懸汪洋之中，土地單薄，遠隔金門、廈門，豈不受制於彼，而能一朝居哉？

translations.literal: If one defended only Penghu, then isolated in the vast ocean, with meager territory and far from Kinmen and Xiamen, how could one avoid being controlled by them and hold the position even for one morning?
translations.idiomatic: If the empire held only Penghu, a lonely outpost in the open sea, with scant land and distant from Kinmen and Xiamen, how could it avoid being dominated by the enemy and hold its ground for even a day?

sentences.zh: 臣思海氛既靖，汰內地溢設之官兵，分防兩處：台灣設總兵一、水師副將一、陸營參將二、兵八千；

translations.literal: Your servant considers that once the maritime threat is pacified, excess troops and officers established inland may be reduced and apportioned to garrison two places: at Taiwan one regional commander, one naval vice commander, two brigade commanders for the land force, eight thousand troops;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant proposes that once the seas are quiet, redundant garrisons inland be thinned and redeployed to guard two posts: in Taiwan, one regional commander, one naval vice commander, two land-force brigade commanders, and eight thousand men;

sentences.zh: 澎湖設水師副將一、兵二千。

translations.literal: At Penghu one naval vice commander, two thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: At Penghu, one naval vice commander and two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 初無添兵增餉之費，已足固守。

translations.literal: At the outset there would be no expense of adding troops or increasing pay, and this would already suffice to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: At no added cost in troops or pay, this would already be enough to hold both places securely.

sentences.zh: 其總兵、副將、參、遊等官，定以二三年轉升內地。

translations.literal: The regional commanders, vice commanders, brigade commanders, regimental commanders, and other officers would be fixed to transfer and be promoted inland within two or three years.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commanders, vice commanders, brigade commanders, regimental commanders, and the rest would rotate inland for promotion every two or three years.

sentences.zh: 其地正賦雜糧，暫行蠲豁。

translations.literal: The land tax and miscellaneous grain levies from that territory would temporarily be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Regular land taxes and miscellaneous grain levies there would be suspended for the time being.

sentences.zh: 駐兵現給全餉，三年後開徵濟用，即不盡資內地轉輸。

translations.literal: Troops stationed there would now receive full pay; after three years collection would begin to supply needs, so the interior would not bear the entire burden of transport.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison would receive full rations at once; only after three years would local levies begin to meet expenses, so the interior would not have to supply everything by transport.

sentences.zh: 蓋籌天下形勢，必期萬全，台灣雖在外島，關四省要害，斷不可棄。

translations.literal: For in planning the empire's strategic situation one must aim for complete security; though Taiwan is an outer island, it concerns vital points of four provinces and must on no account be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: When weighing the empire's strategic position, nothing less than complete security will do. Taiwan may be an offshore island, but it guards the approaches of four provinces and must on no account be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 並繪圖以進。

translations.literal: He also submitted a map along with it.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a map as well.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，下議政王大臣等議，仍未決。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, it was sent down to the Prince Regent, Grand Ministers, and others for deliberation, but still no decision was reached.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, it was referred to the Prince Regent and the Grand Ministers for discussion, but no decision was reached.

sentences.zh: 上召詢廷臣，大學士李霨奏應如瑯請。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned and questioned court officials; Grand Secretary Li Mo memorialized that Lang's request should be followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted the court. Grand Secretary Li Mo advised accepting Lang's proposal.

sentences.zh: 尋蘇拜等疏亦用瑯議，並設縣三、府一、巡道一，上命允行。

translations.literal: Soon Subai and others also memorialized adopting Lang's plan, establishing three counties, one prefecture, and one circuit intendant; the emperor ordered approval.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Subai and his colleagues endorsed Lang's plan as well, proposing one prefecture, three counties, and a circuit intendant. The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 瑯又疏請克塽納土歸誠，應攜族屬與劉國軒、馮錫範及明裔朱桓等俱詣京師，詔授克塽公銜，國軒、錫范伯銜，俱隸上三旗，餘職官及桓等於近省安插墾荒。

translations.literal: Lang again memorialized that since Keshuang had surrendered territory in allegiance, he ought to bring his clansmen together with Liu Guoxuan, Feng Xifan, and the Ming descendant Zhu Huan and others to the capital; an edict conferred on Keshuang the rank of duke, on Guoxuan and Xifan the rank of earl; all were attached to the Upper Three Banners; the remaining officials and Zhu Huan and others were resettled in nearby provinces to reclaim wasteland.
translations.idiomatic: Lang further asked that because Keshuang had surrendered in good faith, he be brought to the capital together with his family, Liu Guoxuan, Feng Xifan, and the Ming descendant Zhu Huan and others. An edict granted Keshuang the rank of duke, Guoxuan and Xifan the rank of earl, and enrolled them all in the Upper Three Banners; the other officials and Zhu Huan and his circle were resettled in neighboring provinces to open new land.

sentences.zh: 复疏請申嚴海禁，稽核貿易商船，命如所議。

translations.literal: He again memorialized requesting strict enforcement of the maritime prohibition and inspection of trading merchant ships; the emperor ordered as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked for tighter enforcement of the sea ban and closer inspection of merchant vessels engaged in trade. The emperor ordered this done as proposed.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，入覲，溫旨慰勞，賞賚優渥。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he came to audience; warm edicts consoled and commended him, and rewards and gifts were lavish.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he came to court. The emperor received him with warm words of praise, and his rewards were generous.

sentences.zh: 上諭瑯曰：「爾前為內大臣十有三年，當時尚有輕爾者。

translations.literal: The emperor addressed Lang, saying: "You previously served as Inner Minister for thirteen years, and at that time there were still those who looked down on you.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Lang: "You served thirteen years as an Inner Minister, and even then there were those who held you in little esteem.

sentences.zh: 惟朕深知爾，待爾甚厚。

translations.literal: Only I knew you well and treated you with great generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Only I knew you truly, and treated you with great favor.

sentences.zh: 後三逆平定，惟海寇潛據台灣為福建害，欲除此寇，非爾不可。

translations.literal: After the Three Feudatories were pacified, only the sea bandits secretly occupying Taiwan harmed Fujian; to eliminate this banditry, none but you would do.
translations.idiomatic: After the Three Feudatories were subdued, only the sea bandits entrenched in Taiwan continued to plague Fujian. To destroy that enemy, there was no one but you.

sentences.zh: 朕特加擢用，爾能不負任使，舉六十年難靖之寇，殄滅無餘。

translations.literal: I specially promoted and employed you, and you did not fail your commission, utterly exterminating bandits hard to pacify for sixty years with none remaining.
translations.idiomatic: I singled you out and raised you up, and you did not fail your charge—you wiped out a foe that had resisted pacification for sixty years, leaving not one survivor.

sentences.zh: 或有言爾恃功驕傲，朕令爾來京。

translations.literal: Some said you relied on your merit and were arrogant; I ordered you to come to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Some said you had grown proud of your achievement. I had you come to the capital.

sentences.zh: 又有言當留勿遣者，朕思寇亂之際，尚用爾勿疑，況天下已平，反疑而勿遣耶？

translations.literal: Others said you should be kept and not sent back; I thought that in the midst of bandit turmoil I still used you without suspicion—now that the realm is pacified, how could I instead suspect you and not send you back?
translations.idiomatic: Others urged that you be kept and not allowed to return. I reasoned that in the midst of rebellion I had employed you without doubting you; now that the realm is at peace, should I doubt you and refuse to let you go back?

sentences.zh: 今命爾復任，宜益加敬慎，以保功名。

translations.literal: Now I order you to resume your post; you ought to be all the more respectful and cautious, to preserve your merit and fame.
translations.idiomatic: Now I appoint you to your post again. Be all the more careful and deferential, and you will keep your honor intact.

sentences.zh: 」瑯奏謝，言：「臣年力已衰，懼勿勝封疆之重。

translations.literal: Lang memorialized in thanks, saying: "Your servant's years and strength have already declined; I fear I cannot bear the weight of frontier duty.
translations.idiomatic: Lang thanked him and said: "I am old now, and I fear I am no longer equal to so heavy a charge on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「將尚智不尚力。

translations.literal: ” The emperor said: “Generals should value wisdom, not brute strength.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, “What a general needs is wit, not muscle.

sentences.zh: 朕用爾亦智耳，豈在手足之力哉？

translations.literal: I employ you for your wisdom as well; how could it depend on the strength of hand and foot?
translations.idiomatic: I put you to use for your mind, not for the strength of your limbs?

sentences.zh: 」命還任。

translations.literal: ” He ordered him to return to his post.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Lang to return to his command.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，卒於官，年七十六，贈太子少傅，賜祭葬，諡襄壯。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year he died in office, at age seventy-six; he was posthumously granted Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, bestowed sacrificial and burial honors, and given the posthumous name Xiangzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year he died in office at seventy-six. The court posthumously made him Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, granted funeral honors, and gave him the posthumous name Xiangzhuang.

sentences.zh: 瑯治軍嚴整，通陣法。

translations.literal: Lang governed troops with strict order and understood battle arrays.
translations.idiomatic: Lang kept his armies in tight discipline and knew how to deploy them.

sentences.zh: 尤善水戰，諳海中風候。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled at naval warfare and understood wind and weather on the sea.
translations.idiomatic: He was above all a master of naval combat and knew the winds and seasons at sea.

sentences.zh: 將出師，值光地請急歸，問瑯曰：「眾皆言南風不利，今乃刻六月出師，何也？

translations.literal: As he was about to take the field, Guangdi urgently petitioned to return home and asked Lang: “All say the south wind is unfavorable; why do you now fix the campaign for the sixth month?
translations.idiomatic: When the fleet was about to sail, Li Guangdi, who had urgently petitioned to go home, asked Lang, “Everyone says a south wind brings disaster—why have you set the departure for the sixth month?

sentences.zh: 」瑯曰：「北風日夜猛。

translations.literal: ” Lang said: “The north wind blows fiercely day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Lang replied, “The north wind blows hard day and night.

sentences.zh: 今攻澎湖，未能一戰克。

translations.literal: Now in attacking Penghu, one cannot take it in a single battle.
translations.idiomatic: If we attack Penghu now, we cannot expect to win at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 風起舟散，將何以戰？

translations.literal: When the wind rises the ships scatter—how then shall one fight?
translations.idiomatic: Once the wind rises the fleet will scatter—what battle could we fight then?

sentences.zh: 夏至前後二十餘日，風微，夜尤靜，可聚泊大洋。

translations.literal: For more than twenty days before and after the summer solstice, the wind is light and the nights especially calm; one can gather and anchor on the open ocean.
translations.idiomatic: For some twenty days around the summer solstice the winds are mild and the nights especially still—we can mass the fleet on the open sea.

sentences.zh: 觀釁而動，不過七日，舉之必矣。

translations.literal: Watch for the opportune moment and strike; within seven days the affair will certainly be settled.
translations.idiomatic: We wait for the opening and strike—in no more than seven days the prize will surely be ours.

sentences.zh: 即偶有颶風，此則天意，非人慮所及。

translations.literal: Even if a hurricane should occasionally arise, that is Heaven's will, not within human foresight.
translations.idiomatic: If a typhoon should come, that is Heaven's decree, beyond what planning can guard against.

sentences.zh: 鄭氏將劉國軒最驍，以他將守澎湖，雖敗，彼必再戰。

translations.literal: Of Zheng's generals, Liu Guoxuan is the fiercest; if another general holds Penghu, though defeated, they will surely fight again.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guoxuan is the boldest of the Zheng commanders. If someone else holds Penghu, defeat will only bring another battle.

sentences.zh: 今以國軒守，敗則膽落，台灣可​​不戰而下。

translations.literal: Now with Guoxuan left to defend it, once defeated his courage will fail, and Taiwan can be taken without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Leave Guoxuan in command, and once he is beaten his nerve will break—Taiwan will fall without another fight.

sentences.zh: 」及戰，雲起東南，國軒望見，謂颶作，喜甚。

translations.literal: ” When battle came, clouds rose in the southeast; Guoxuan saw them, said a hurricane was forming, and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When battle was joined, clouds piled up in the southeast. Guoxuan saw them, thought a typhoon was rising, and rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 俄，雷聲殷殷，國軒推案起曰：「天命矣！

translations.literal: Before long thunder rolled deeply; Guoxuan pushed aside his table and rose, saying: “Heaven has decreed it!
translations.idiomatic: Then thunder rolled across the sky. Guoxuan shoved back his desk and stood, crying, “This is Heaven's judgment!

sentences.zh: 今且敗。

translations.literal: We are about to be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: We are lost today.

sentences.zh: 」人謂瑯必報父仇，將致毒於鄭氏。

translations.literal: ” People said Lang would surely avenge his father's wrong and would visit cruelty upon the Zheng clan.
translations.idiomatic: People expected Lang to avenge his father and visit harsh punishment on the Zheng family.

sentences.zh: 瑯曰：「絕島新附，一有誅戮，恐人情反側。

translations.literal: Lang said: “The outer island has newly submitted; were there executions, I fear the people's hearts would turn rebellious.
translations.idiomatic: Lang said, “Taiwan has only just submitted. Any large-scale killing would turn the people against us.

sentences.zh: 吾所以銜卹茹痛者，為國事重，不敢顧私也。

translations.literal: The reason I hold grief in my breast and swallow pain is that state affairs weigh heavier; I dare not heed private ends.
translations.idiomatic: I swallow my grief because the state's need comes first—I dare not indulge private vengeance.

sentences.zh: 」子世綸、世驃，自有傳；

translations.literal: ” His sons Shilun and Shipiao have their own biographies;
translations.idiomatic: His sons Shilun and Shipiao are recorded in separate biographies;

sentences.zh: 世範，襲爵。

translations.literal: Shifan inherited the marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: =朱天貴=朱天貴，福建莆田人。

translations.literal: =Zhu Tiangui= Zhu Tiangui was a native of Putian in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tiangui came from Putian in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 初為鄭錦將。

translations.literal: At first he was a general under Zheng Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He had originally served Zheng Jing as a general.

sentences.zh: 康熙十九年，師下海壇，以所部二萬人、舟三百來降，授平陽總兵。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Kangxi, when the army descended on Haitan, he came over with his division of twenty thousand men and three hundred ships and was appointed regional commander of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of the Kangxi reign, when imperial forces moved against Haitan, he defected with twenty thousand troops and three hundred vessels and was made regional commander of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 瑯攻澎湖，天貴以師會。

translations.literal: When Lang attacked Penghu, Tiangui joined with his forces.
translations.idiomatic: When Lang besieged Penghu, Tiangui brought his troops to join him.

sentences.zh: 國軒拒戰，天貴以十二舟薄敵壘，焚其舟，殺傷甚眾，戰益力，俄，中飛砲僕舟中，猶大呼殺賊，遂卒，贈太子少保，諡忠壯。

translations.literal: Guoxuan resisted; Tiangui with twelve ships pressed close to the enemy stockade, burned their ships, killed and wounded a great many, and fought with growing vigor; before long a flying cannonball struck him and he fell in his ship, yet still shouted to kill the bandits, then died. He was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Zhongzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxuan met him in battle. Tiangui closed on the enemy stockade with twelve ships, set their vessels afire, and inflicted heavy casualties, fighting all the harder as the action wore on. A cannonball suddenly struck him down on deck; he still roared to slay the rebels before he died. The court posthumously made him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and gave him the posthumous name Zhongzhuang.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：台灣平，瑯專其功。

translations.literal: =【Commentary】= The commentary says: When Taiwan was pacified, Lang monopolized the credit.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: When Taiwan was pacified, Lang claimed the whole victory for himself.

sentences.zh: 然啟聖、興祚經營規畫，戡定諸郡縣。

translations.literal: Yet Qisheng and Xingzuo had managed and planned affairs, pacifying the various prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Qisheng and Xingzuo had laid the groundwork and brought the prefectures and counties under control.

sentences.zh: 及金、廈既下，鄭氏僅有台澎，遂聚而殲。

translations.literal: When Jinmen and Xiamen had already fallen, the Zheng clan held only Taiwan and Penghu, and they were gathered together and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Jinmen and Xiamen had fallen, the Zheng holdouts were confined to Taiwan and Penghu—and there they were cornered and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 先事之勞，何可泯也？

translations.literal: The labor of what went before—how could it be erased?
translations.idiomatic: Can the work that came before be simply forgotten?

sentences.zh: 及瑯出師，啟聖、興祚欲與同進，瑯遽疏言未奉督撫同進之命。

translations.literal: When Lang took the field, Qisheng and Xingzuo wished to advance together; Lang hastily memorialized that he had received no order from the governor-general and commissioners to advance together.
translations.idiomatic: When Lang sailed, Qisheng and Xingzuo wanted to go with him. Lang immediately memorialized that he had no orders for the governor-general and provincial commissioners to join the advance.

sentences.zh: 上命啟聖同瑯進取，止興祚毋行。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Qisheng to advance with Lang to take the objective, and forbade Xingzuo to go.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Qisheng to join Lang in the campaign but forbade Xingzuo to take the field.

sentences.zh: 既克，啟聖告捷疏後瑯至，賞不及，鬱鬱發病卒。

translations.literal: After the victory, Qisheng's report of triumph arrived after Lang's; his reward did not match his merit; he fell ill from dejection and died.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory, Qisheng's victory report reached the court after Lang's. He was passed over for rewards, sank into gloom, took ill, and died.

sentences.zh: 功名之際，有難言之矣。

translations.literal: At the juncture of fame and reward, there are matters hard to speak plainly of.
translations.idiomatic: Where merit meets reward, some things cannot easily be said aloud.

sentences.zh: 大敵在前，將帥內相競，審擇堅任，一戰而克。

translations.literal: With a great enemy before them, the generals competed among themselves; the sovereign chose carefully and entrusted firmly, and took it in a single battle.
translations.idiomatic: With the great enemy before them, the commanders jockeyed among themselves—yet the sovereign chose well, stood firm in his appointment, and won in a single campaign.

sentences.zh: 非聖祖善馭群材，曷能有此哉？

translations.literal: If the Sacred Ancestor had not been skilled at harnessing all talents, how could there have been this?
translations.idiomatic: Without the Sacred Ancestor's gift for wielding men of ability, how could such a victory have been achieved?
